context: WebGL-instanced treemap of 5,000 synthetic leaves across 10 sectors, toggling between Revenue and Headcount layouts with 800ms animated interpolation; SVG overlay for sector labels, tooltip on hover.
first_impression: Structurally honest treemap with correct proportional area encoding in both layout states and clear labeling of each mode.
what_works: Area encoding is mathematically correct — d3.hierarchy().sum() derives tile sizes directly from data with no magic-number domains; cross-layout identity is maintained via data-reference keying (hcMap), so each leaf tracks correctly between Revenue and Headcount states.
what_doesnt: Animated intermediate frames are geometrically interpolated between two independent treemap computations, so transitional cell sizes represent no meaningful data value (inherent limitation of treemap morphing, not deception); canvas dimensions are hardcoded at 1200×800 rather than derived from container, acceptable for synthetic demo but would break scale invariance on resize.
